content:
Elliot Price: Dropping the IA proposal for Quickstart Templates review. Main questions: where in left nav, how to avoid duplicating SDK guides, and how we route users from SDK docs -> templates. Doc: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/quickstarts-ia-proposal (WIP)

Wei Chen: skimmed. +1 to calling it “Quickstart Templates” not just “Templates” (less generic). But nav placement feels tricky: under “Get started” vs under “Guides”? I worry people expect “Quickstart” = 5 min snippet, whereas these are full apps.

Monica Patel: from DevEx side we want it discoverable from day 0. Users are landing on SDK pages and missing the templates entirely. I’d put it in nav near SDKs, but we should make the copy explicit: “production-minded starter apps”.

Renee Sullivan: +1. In user interviews folks literally asked “do you have a reference app?” after reading SDK docs. If it’s buried under Get started they won’t find it.

Elliot Price: Current strawman:
- Get started
  - Quickstart (API call)
  - Quickstart Templates
    - RAG + Agents (Python)
    - RAG + Agents (TypeScript)
  - Deployments
- SDKs
  - Python
  - TypeScript
  - Go
- Guides
  - RAG
  - Agents (tool calling)
  - Observability

Wei Chen: Duplication risk: “Guides > RAG” will overlap with “RAG + Agents template walkthrough”. How do we keep them distinct?

Monica Patel: I think template walkthrough should be “how to run this repo and what knobs exist” (env vars, retries, evals, OTel). Guides should stay conceptual / portable. Like: retrieval patterns, chunking tradeoffs, prompt injection mitigations, etc.

Henry Cho: That makes sense, but users don’t always distinguish “guide vs template”. Maybe we add a callout at top of Guides: “Want a working app? Start with the RAG + Agents quickstart template” linking over.

Elliot Price: yep. Also on SDK pages: a module-level banner: “Looking for an end-to-end app? Try Quickstart Templates” with the two language options.

Nikhil Sharma: PM note: routing from SDK docs is key for activation metrics. If we do a banner/callout, can we ensure it’s consistent across languages? Also avoid mentioning “agents” too prominently without definition (we got confusion in #product last week).

Wei Chen: Terminology: “Agents” is overloaded. In docs we can say “tool-calling workflow (agent loop)” and reserve “agent” as shorthand. We should add a short glossary blurb near the template intro.

Monica Patel: +1. In the template README we already use “agent loop” more than “agents” per the docs thread feedback.

Allison Grant: On nav placement: I’d avoid putting Templates under “SDKs”. It’s not an SDK artifact, and it’ll feel like an appendix. “Get started” is the right mental model. But we must link from SDK pages.

Renee Sullivan: I’m ok with Get started as long as it’s not below the fold / collapsed. Could we pin “Quickstart Templates” near the top of Get started (right after Quickstart)?

Elliot Price: That’s my preference. Another issue: “Deployments” page might overlap with template deployment recipes (Docker/Fly/k8s). I don’t want two sources of truth.

Wei Chen: Suggestion: Templates have a “Deployment” section but it links out to the canonical Deployments docs. Template content should be “how to run this template on X” + minimal, and any deeper “what’s Dedicated vs Private” lives in Deployments.

Monica Patel: Agree. Template should include: local dev + Docker Compose + “production notes” (env vars, secrets, collector). For actual Hosted/Dedicated/Private decisioning, send them to Deployments.

Henry Cho: Also: on the template page, we should have a small box: “Hosted API default; Dedicated/Private supported” with links. But avoid implying templates magically configure Private networking etc.

Elliot Price: yep. I’ll add a “Supported deployment modes” section with explicit caveats:
- Hosted: works out of the box
- Dedicated: works with endpoint + auth changes
- Private/VPC: works, but you bring networking + collector endpoint

Nikhil Sharma: Another duplication risk: “Get started > Quickstart” vs “Quickstart Templates”. We should keep Quickstart as the 60-second curl/SDK snippet. Templates is “clone/init + run”. We need that distinction in the intro paragraph.

Wei Chen: maybe a top-level “Choose your start” page under Get started?
1) “Make your first request” (curl/SDK)
2) “Start from an app template” (RAG + tool-calling)
3) “Deploy to production” (deployment options)

Elliot Price: I like, but might be scope creep for this PR. Could do v2. For now, we can add a short intro on the Templates landing page: “If you’re looking for a single API call, use Quickstart.”

Renee Sullivan: +1 keep it simple for launch.

Allison Grant: One more: observability. We should make sure templates pages are cross-linked from Observability docs. People search “OpenTelemetry” and never see templates.

Monica Patel: We have a “Verify observability” script and standard span names. If docs adds a section “Quickstart template instrumentation conventions” we can link both ways.

Elliot Price: I’ll add a “Observability (OTel)” subsection on the template pages with:
- what signals it emits
- how to run local collector
- link to the full Observability Hooks Reference

Wei Chen: Also add a “Troubleshooting” link in nav under Templates? Or keep it in Templates landing page only.

Elliot Price: I was thinking Templates section includes:
- Overview
- RAG + tool-calling (Python)
- RAG + tool-calling (TypeScript)
- Troubleshooting
- Observability reference (or keep that under Observability)

Nikhil Sharma: Troubleshooting under Templates seems good. It’s a high-intent path.

Henry Cho: +1. Also include “Common errors: 401/429/timeouts/tool schema” on that page, and route to SDK error docs where applicable.

Monica Patel: careful: if troubleshooting references SDK errors, make sure we don’t create a circular maze. Maybe each error section has:
- What it means
- Fix in template config
- “If you’re using the SDK directly, see …” link

Elliot Price: makes sense.

Wei Chen: Action items I’m hearing:
1) Keep Templates in Get started, high placement.
2) Add consistent callouts on all SDK pages linking to Templates.
3) Split conceptual guides vs template walkthroughs (explicit language).
4) Avoid duplicating Deployment docs; templates link to canonical pages.
5) Add glossary note for “agent loop / tool calling”.

Elliot Price: yup. I’ll update the IA doc + PR accordingly. Targeting PR this afternoon (PR-841 is the nav one). I’ll @ you for review.

Talia Benson: timeline check: can we lock nav/IA by EOW? It’s gating the docs launch checklist.

Elliot Price: yes, if we keep scope to nav + landing page + SDK callouts. Defer “Choose your start” page.

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup: works for me.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: and please ping me on any observability wording so we don’t promise high-cardinality attributes etc.

Monica Patel: I’ll review the SDK callout copy once it’s in. Want to align w/ what the CLI actually does (init/doctor).

Elliot Price: cool. I’m taking this thread as approval to proceed w/ “Get started > Quickstart Templates” + SDK callouts. Will post updated links shortly.
